countries.name: Indonesia
countries.description: Indonesian music blends gamelan and regional folk instruments with pop and dangdut; artists often mix traditional scales and percussion with modern production.
tasks: Listen to 'Bento' and note the interplay between acoustic guitar and narrative lyrics.
Compare a dangdut rhythm with a modern Indonesian pop track and note percussion differences.

countries.name: Malaysia
countries.description: Malaysia mixes Malay melodic modes and traditional percussion with pop, rock and R&B; multilingual lyrics are common and give rise to varied textures.
tasks: Listen to P. Ramlee to hear classic Malay film-song phrasing.
Pick a Yuna song and observe the production choices that give it international pop appeal.

countries.name: Chile
countries.description: Chilean music often blends Andean folk instruments and protest-song traditions with contemporary indie and pop influences.
examples: Violeta Parra - Gracias a la Vida
Los Bunkers - Llueve Sobre La Ciudad
tasks: Listen to 'Gracias a la Vida' and focus on the lyrical storytelling.
Compare an Andean melody to a modern Chilean indie arrangement.

countries.name: Bolivia
countries.description: Bolivian music centers Andean wind instruments and communal dance forms; contemporary artists blend these with cumbia, pop and fusion genres.
tasks: Listen for panpipe and charango textures and how they outline melody.
Explore a modern Bolivian fusion track and note how traditional instruments are mixed with electronic elements.

countries.name: Peru
countries.description: Peruvian music ranges from Afro-Peruvian coastal styles to highland huaynos; it's a rich fusion of rhythmic variety and melodic modes.
tasks: Listen for call-and-response patterns in Afro-Peruvian songs.
Compare coastal rhythms to highland huayno structures.

countries.name: South Korea
countries.description: South Korea's scene includes highly produced K-pop idols, intimate ballads and an active indie/hip-hop underground; production and visual concepts are central.
tasks: Compare a K-pop single's arrangement to a Korean indie acoustic track.
Note how vocal layering and production create the polished K-pop sound.

countries.name: Japan
countries.description: Japanese music covers traditional enka, city pop, J-pop, and experimental electronic scenes; each has distinct melodic and production conventions.
tasks: Listen to 'First Love' and note melody and phrasing typical of J-pop ballads.
Compare city pop production to modern synth-pop arrangements.

countries.name: Brazil
countries.description: Brazilian music emphasizes syncopated rhythms and rich percussion (samba, bossa nova); modern artists fuse these roots with pop, rock and electronic styles.
tasks: Compare a samba rhythm's groove to a bossa nova's laid-back syncopation.
Listen for percussion layering and how it drives dance styles.

countries.name: Nigeria
countries.description: Nigeria is the birthplace of Afrobeats and rich popular music traditions; contemporary producers blend highlife, hip-hop and pop into infectious grooves.
tasks: Listen to the rhythmic patterns in Afrobeats and how bass and percussion interact.
Compare older highlife arrangements to modern Afrobeats production.

countries.name: United States
countries.description: The U.S. shaped many global genres (jazz, blues, rock, hip-hop, country); regional scenes and historic movements have lasting influence on modern music.
tasks: Listen to a jazz standard focusing on improvisation and form.
Compare early blues structures to modern rock songwriting.
